title: Ramesses the Great
objective: After this level you can explain why Ramesses II is remembered as a great builder.
summary: Ramesses II reigned for 66 years and put up more monuments and statues than any other pharaoh, recarving older statues as his own.

cards.headline: A famous poem made Ramesses II the symbol of forgotten power.
cards.body: Shelley’s sonnet “Ozymandias,” published in 1818, describes a ruined statue of Ramesses II, its boastful inscription standing in empty desert. The irony: few pharaohs ever worked harder at being remembered.

cards.headline: Sixty-six years
cards.body: Ramesses II, son of Seti I, reigned from 1279 to 1213 BCE: 66 years, one of the longest reigns in Egyptian history. He had more than 100 children and outlived many of them. Anyone younger than about 66 at his death had never known another king. That’s a lot of time to build.

cards.headline: The builder king
cards.body: And build he did: the Ramesseum, his great temple at Thebes; two temples at Abu Simbel; a new capital called Per-Ramessu; and work on Karnak’s Hypostyle Hall and at Abydos. He put up more monuments and statues than any other pharaoh. Walk around Egypt today and his face keeps turning up.
cards.callout: More monuments and statues than any other pharaoh

cards.headline: Ramesses was here
cards.body: Not all of it was new. A statue in Turin’s Museo Egizio was made for an earlier king, probably Amenhotep II. Ramesses’ sculptors recarved its face to look like his official portrait and put his name on its belt. If you couldn’t build it, you could still sign it.

mascot.line: Ancient Egypt’s most prolific builder was also its most confident autographer.

cards.fact: The head that inspired “Ozymandias” weighs 7.25 tons.
cards.context: It is a granite fragment of a colossal Ramesses statue from the Ramesseum, now in the British Museum. News that it was about to reach England in 1818 set Shelley writing. The poem mocks a forgotten king, yet here we are, still reading his name.

cards.headline: Ramesses the Great: met
learned: Ramesses II reigned 66 years, from 1279 to 1213 BCE
He built the Ramesseum, Abu Simbel and a new capital
He put up more monuments and statues than any other pharaoh
He also recarved older kings’ statues as his own

questions.prompt: About how long did Ramesses II reign?

options.label: About 10 years
options.rationale: That is closer to Tutankhamun’s reign.

questions.explanation: He reigned from 1279 to 1213 BCE, 66 years, one of the longest reigns in Egyptian history.

questions.prompt: What did Ramesses II’s sculptors do to the statue now in Turin’s Museo Egizio?

options.label: Moved it from Abu Simbel to Italy for safekeeping
options.rationale: It went to Turin much later.

options.label: Recarved an earlier king’s statue and added his name
Covered it in gold leaf
options.rationale: The change was to its face and name.

questions.explanation: The statue was made for an earlier king, probably Amenhotep II; Ramesses had its face recarved and his name added.

questions.prompt: Tutankhamun is famous mainly for a surviving tomb. What is Ramesses II remembered for?

options.label: A tomb found untouched
options.rationale: That describes Tutankhamun, more or less.

options.label: Building more monuments and statues than any other pharaoh
Moving Egypt’s capital out of Egypt and into Greece
options.rationale: His new capital, Per-Ramessu, was in Egypt.

questions.explanation: Tutankhamun’s fame came from what survived him; Ramesses made his own, in stone, across Egypt.
